title: Distribution-Aware End-to-End Embedding for Streaming Numerical Features in Click-Through Rate Prediction

problem.claim: The task is to develop effective numerical-feature embeddings for click-through rate prediction in streaming settings.

gap.claim: Static binning can cause semantic drift during boundary updates, while neural embedding methods may discard distributional information; streaming non-i.i.d. data and neglected context dependency further complicate distribution-aware embedding.

contributions.claim: DAES is an end-to-end framework that integrates distributional information with adaptive modulation for numerical feature embedding in streaming training scenarios.
DAES introduces reservoir-sampling-based distribution estimation and two field-aware distribution modulation strategies.
DAES has been fully deployed on a leading short-video platform.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Offline and online experiments reportedly show that DAES significantly outperforms existing approaches.
A/B tests reportedly reveal a 2.307% lift in advertiser value.
The framework is reportedly deployed on a leading short-video platform with hundreds of millions of daily active users.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies numerical feature embedding for click-through rate prediction in streaming environments.

Existing static and neural approaches respectively risk semantic drift or loss of explicit distributional information, while streaming non-i.i.d. conditions and context dependency create additional challenges.
DAES integrates distributional information with adaptive modulation and uses reservoir sampling plus field-aware modulation strategies.
The authors report offline, online, and A/B-test results and production deployment.

source_observation.claim: Streaming numerical features can require distribution estimation and field-aware modulation because distribution context may vary across fields and streaming data may violate i.i.d. assumptions.

interpretation.claim: Embedding methods for streaming numerical features should account for both evolving distributions and feature-field semantics.

application.claim: Consider combining online distribution estimation with field-specific modulation in streaming prediction systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach is necessary or beneficial outside streaming numerical-feature settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify datasets, baseline identities, metric definitions, or experimental configurations.
The abstract does not provide implementation details, deployment constraints, or statistical details for the reported A/B-test lift.
